notes: The manuscript introduces the case of hat M!_{0,5} or hat M_{0,I}, draws three codimension columns, and states that there are ten divisors at infinity, each a copy of hat M!_{0,4}; an inserted refinement identifies a divisor with hat M_{0,I″(3)amalg(*)} and a projective line over Z. These geometric identifications were read as manuscript claims, not proved in this run. An independent finite enumeration on I={0,1,2,3,4} produced ten two-element subsets, three disjoint two-element partners for every subset, fifteen unordered disjoint pairs, and fifteen distinct partitions with block-size multiset (1,2,2). It also counted thirty ordered incidences and verified 30/2=15. This checks the combinatorial counts in the prose and arrow labels, not the geometric correspondence between these sets and boundary strata.

The manuscript states that two such divisors meet exactly when their two-element subsets are disjoint, and describes the resulting partition as I′, I″, and I minus their union. The set partitions constructed in the finite enumeration have this form. The geometric intersection criterion itself was carried as background and was not independently established. The phi-like glyph is transcribed from its long-stemmed loop shape, not chosen to make the criterion true.

The left marginal definition reads P^1_{I″} def = P^1_Z wedge_subS3 Isom({0,1,infinity},I″). The blind audit and a complete rotated crop establish that the sloping tuple continues this marginal formula; it is not an independent prose insertion. The capped I and following s/o/m strokes replace the first tentative tilde-I reading. These are source-reading corrections; the associated construction has not been proved.

The lower paragraph invokes the combinatorial study of the icosahedron and claims that choosing an orientation of I determines an oriented icosahedron, then uses the abbreviation icos. with the word gauche, resolved in the blind audit. This orientation/icosahedron claim was read but not proved or checked against external material. The paragraph continues to the ten elements of P_2(I), using the uncertain written abbreviation elmts|elts and stops with the unfinished insertion ou (par and a canceled tentative correspon-.

Remaining limits include de/des, de/le, the overworked final graph index, avait/aurait, both canceled formula trials, the possible cancellation of the second sss, choisissant/choisissons, the final elmts/elts abbreviation, and the crossed en ordre/correspon-.
